header: A plant document (a JO Manual) full screen over the card, at the cited page: I use the same layer as the announcement PDF (ViewerShell; closes with the cross and Escape; the page behind keeps its scroll position), with

* a strip above the PDF that names the manual, says "page 34 of 102" and has two buttons: "Title page" (the first page, as proof that it is the right manual) and "Cited page" (back to the page the card cited);
* the PDF itself below, opened at the page (the browser's own viewer takes #page=; the page numbers the card cites are the PDF's own, checked by script).

For an internal document (a JO Manual) the viewer first asks our route (?info=1): signed in -> the PDF; not signed in (401) -> "Sign in to read this document" with a Sign in button (it opens the intranet's sign-in window, and the document opens by itself once the reader is signed in); not uploaded yet (404) -> says so. I record nothing about who opened what. `DocViewerContext` lets any source line of the card open it (SourceLine in DspHistoryCard.tsx); without the provider (a test, a page outside the card) a page link is an ordinary link to the route.

behaviours: the route's answer decides the state: 200 ready, 401 sign in, 404 not uploaded, anything else an error
the PDF opens at the cited page, thumbnails closed, 150%: /api/history-docs/jo-086#page=34&navpanes=0&zoom=150 (a page below 1 is page 1)
signed in: the page view is there at that page (the manual's page drawn with the quote marked, not the whole file in a frame), and the strip names the manual and says 'page 34 of 102'
the strip has Previous page and Next page (not Previous on page 1, not Next on the last page) and 'Open the whole manual', a link to the browser's own viewer at that page
on the cited page the strip offers 'Title page' (the proof that it is the right manual) and not 'Cited page'; on the title page it offers 'Cited page' and not 'Title page'; elsewhere both
the DSP manual says its own length: 'page 12 of 49'
not signed in: no PDF, a notice that says to sign in and why (internal), and a Sign in button
without a way to open the sign-in window there is the notice but no button
not uploaded, checking and error each say so, and show no PDF
a published PDF whose copy is not in storage yet says so and offers the publisher's own file at the cited page meanwhile; an internal manual offers nothing of the kind
a published PDF's strip says 'page 36' without a total until the document is read, then 'page 36 of 70'; 'Open the whole document' leads to the publisher's file at that page

while the reader is away signing in the viewer's layer is not drawn (the sign-in window must be on top of everything, and the layer is above the search window); it is drawn again afterwards, and never without an open document
the layer is the app's own full-screen viewer: closable, on top of the search window, taking Escape for itself
